title: Interior Ministry police and firefighters’ salary rally
location: Sofia, St Sedmochislenitsi garden and march to government institutions
organizer: Interior Ministry Employees Trade Union Federation (reported); firefighters also present.
threshold_50_evidence: No number of attendees. A quoted union membership figure is not used as rally turnout.

start_date.summary: BNT dates the executed rally to 8 November and says employees assembled around midday.

location.summary: Gathering in Sofia at the St Sedmochislenitsi church garden; procession to Finance Ministry, Council of Ministers and Parliament.

demands.summary: Police and firefighters sought 30% salary increases and objected to the 15% offer/frontline-pay exclusion.

organizer.summary: BNT attributes the demonstration to police employees and the Interior Ministry employees’ union.

participants.summary: The report says police from across the country, but gives no number at the rally; “across the country” is not a size count.

threshold_50.summary: No simultaneous participant count or qualifying qualitative lower bound is supplied.

protester_violence.summary: No relevant body evidence of protester violence; remains unknown.

notes: This was an executed physical rally. Related to the October 21 Varna wage action and later November 29 national rally by issue, but those dates are not automatically merged.
open_questions: Can rally turnout at Sofia be verified?
Is this a new episode or part of the October wage-action series?

title: Transport-carrier and taxi protest in Sofia, with taxi action continuing next day
organizer: Transport-carrier/taxi organizations; precise association is unresolved.
participants_original: Buses and company yellow taxi vehicles; no attendee count
threshold_50_evidence: Physical action is confirmed; no reported participant number establishes 50. Search-only BNT wording is retained as a follow-up lead, not sufficient proof.

start_date.summary: Flagman reports the executed transport/taxi rally on 25 November. BNT’s search header also dates the event, but the exact body open timed out.

location.summary: Flagman places transport/taxi vehicles on Tsar Osvoboditel near Parliament and the Triangle of Power.

demands.summary: Carriers and taxi drivers sought criminalization of unlicensed passenger transport in response to a parliamentary veto of amendments.

organizer.summary: The article calls this an announced mass action by transport carriers and taxi drivers; specific association identity is not established in this page.

participants.summary: Flagman notes buses and company taxis and labels the action large-scale, but provides no count. BNT search header says hundreds of taxis and buses but its body timed out; that header is not accepted as verified threshold evidence.

threshold_50.summary: The opened Flagman report confirms vehicles and a blockade, but no count or clear minimum of 50; BNT header is search-only and not relied on for eligibility.

protester_violence.summary: No transport-group violence is described; remains unknown.

notes: Flagman describes a separate anti-COVID-restrictions gathering (“tens”) that later physically overlapped with the transport action. Do not count the anti-restriction crowd as taxi/carrier participants. NOVA/BNT report taxi street action on 26 November as a second consecutive day; included here as a two-day sequence, but the group/demand boundary and subsequent December recurrence remain open.
open_questions: Was the transport/taxi gathering at least 50 simultaneously?
Do the 25 and 26 November actions form one episode or two?
Is the December tariff action a renewal or a separate episode?

title: Second national police/firefighter salary protest
location: Sofia, Alexander I / National Assembly square
organizer: Interior Ministry employees’ union as named in Sega; NOVA reports national employee protest.
threshold_50_evidence: Rally execution and nationwide organizing are described, but no headcount or clear crowd-size minimum is given.

start_date.summary: NOVA and Sega date the second national rally to 29 November.

location.summary: Main demonstration was in central Sofia near Alexander I and the new Parliament.

demands.summary: Police and firefighters maintained a demand for a 30% pay rise after a 15% offer.

organizer.summary: Sega attributes organization to the Interior Ministry employees’ union; it cites BNR for some reporting, so is not treated as independent confirmation.

participants.summary: The pages do not report an attendance number; “from different regions” is not a count.

threshold_50.summary: No body evidence establishes 50 simultaneous participants.

protester_violence.summary: No violence by the police protesters is reported; unknown.

notes: NOVA’s story footer credits BGNES and Sega explicitly cites BNR for some details; these are not counted as independent corroboration. The counter-protest described by Sega is a separate action, not merged into this candidate.
open_questions: Can a crowd count be obtained?
Should this be a continuation of the October/November police-pay sequence?

title: Anti-lockdown demonstration outside Council of Ministers
location: Sofia, Council of Ministers / government triangle
threshold_50_evidence: The report describes tens; this does not establish 50 or more.

start_date.summary: Flagman dates this assembly to 25 November; it says organizers had mobilized from the previous day, but exact earlier action is not established.

location.summary: The anti-restrictions group assembled before the Council of Ministers in Sofia.

demands.summary: Participants opposed newly imposed COVID restrictions; this is a domestic policy demand.

participants.summary: Flagman describes “tens” of participants, without a bounded count.

threshold_50.summary: “Tens” does not establish a minimum of 50.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is described; unknown.

notes: Separate from the taxi/carrier protest nearby. Flagman says the two gatherings later physically merged, but their organizers and demands remain distinct.
open_questions: Was attendance at this gathering 50 or more?
Was there a prior public action on 24 November?

title: Varna municipal-transit conductors protest planned layoffs
location: Varna, municipal public-transport context (specific venue unresolved)
threshold_50_evidence: The 270 figure concerns workers receiving notices, not attendees; attendance threshold unknown.

start_date.summary: BNT’s 2 December article links a prior conductor protest dated 23 November; the contemporaneous date is therefore reported in a later article.

location.summary: BNT and Eurocom locate the affected conductors in Varna public transport.

demands.summary: Conductors sought delay of mass layoffs during the emergency period and discussion of fair compensation/retraining/reassignment.

organizer.summary: The Autonomous Workers Confederation supported the action; exact local organizer structure is not fully stated.

participants.summary: More than 270 employees received dismissal notices; this is affected workforce, not demonstrators. Protest attendance is not reported.

threshold_50.summary: No report gives a count of protest attendees.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence described; remains unknown.

notes: State target is unresolved: immediate grievance concerns a municipal transit operator/e-ticketing and layoffs, while some demands refer to the state of emergency. Do not code a purely employer dispute as state-directed without clarifying policy responsibility. December 2/3 are documented repeat actions in December continuation records.
open_questions: Did a simultaneous group of 50+ assemble?
Was the demand directed to state policy or to the employer/municipal company?
Was 23 November the first qualifying public action?

title: Varna restaurant workers protest COVID-lockdown impacts
organizer: Committee of Bulgarian Chefs / Autonomous Workers’ Confederation (report attribution; exact co-organizer role unresolved).
threshold_50_evidence: Public gathering is reported, but no number/qualitative lower bound establishes 50.

start_date.summary: Peoples Dispatch dates the restaurant/chef workers’ action to Friday 27 November.

location.summary: The report says restaurant workers protested in front of Varna’s municipal office.

demands.summary: Workers sought support/minimum-income measures due to new national COVID restrictions on restaurants and other businesses.

organizer.summary: The report names the Committee of Bulgarian Chefs and Autonomous Workers’ Confederation in relation to the calls/actions.

threshold_50.summary: No crowd count or clear minimum of 50 appears in the read passage.

notes: Kept separate from bus conductors: location is proximate, but groups and demands differ. The article was published 1 December and retrospectively dates the action; it does not document a December gathering.
open_questions: Was the public policy demand adopted by the participants rather than only their union?
